label: Church organ, principal chorus, recorded in its building
_takes: The corpus is eleven isolated notes at one velocity, so nothing in it hears what happens between notes or between ranks: a hold long enough for the chorus to beat against itself, a slur where the wind never restarts, the swell box, and a jump across the compass where the mixture changes what a note is made of. `sustained` is the set for anything blown, and its five phrases land on an organ's own controls rather than on a wind player's - expression here is a real swell pedal and not a dynamic, and a repeated note is a key attack and not a tongue. What it has no phrase for is a chord, which is where a chorus's tuning against itself is most audible; that needs a set of its own.
audition_title: libsonare church organ vs the sampled reference
_registration:
The single most important property, and the one nothing downstream can recover from. libsonare's program 19 bank 0 is a six-rank principal chorus - 16', 8', 4', 2 2/3', 2', 1 3/5', no reeds. `rank_count` is not among the patch's fittable fields, so the NUMBER of ranks is fixed; each rank's `footage_mult` is one, bounded 0.25 to 16, so the pitches are not. That asymmetry is the thing to hold onto in a fit: a footage the reference has and the model does not is reachable, and reaching for it is almost always the wrong move, because a fitter given six free footages will land on whatever additive stack fits eleven notes rather than on a chorus. Pin `footage_mult` unless the intent is explicitly to re-voice the registration, and change the levels and brightnesses instead.

On a SAMPLED reference the registration is not a setting at all - it was chosen when the samples were recorded, and no control reaches it - so the requirement is met by selecting a slot and measuring it, never by setting one. Select it on the partial ladder rather than on the slot's name: on the rack this was captured from, a slot reading h3 at -29 dB and h5 at -78 dB at C4 has no mutation ranks at all and is a solo registration whatever it is called, while the two kept here carry every ratio from h1 to h8. A ratio the model has no rank for is the thing to watch: h6 and h8 are strong in both slots and libsonare has no 1 1/3' or 1' rank, so they have to arrive as the upper harmonics of the ranks it does have, which is the `brightness` knobs' job and not the levels'.
_other_registrations: Program 19 has two more, reachable with `--bank`: bank 8 is three flute ranks and bank 16 a full organ with reeds. Each is its own patch with its own knobs, so each wants its own capture with the reference registered to match - this one is bank 0. `autofit.py --program 19 --dump-knobs` lists the banks a program has.
registration: Two sampled principal choruses, selected on their partial ladders rather than set: both carry every ratio h1 to h8 across the compass, and differ in where the weight sits - `plenum-a` is upperwork-forward, `plenum-b` fundamental-forward. Neither is a stop list anyone chose here, and neither is claimed to be exactly 16' + 8' + 4' + 2 2/3' + 2' + 1 3/5'; what is claimed is that no ratio in either is unreachable by the six ranks libsonare has.
_dry: An organ is voiced for its building - the room is the instrument, not an effect on it - so the capture keeps it. `dry` is off, which means the plugin's own effect sections are left as the preset set them. The consequence downstream is that the room has to be treated as a nuisance parameter rather than ignored: `autofit` measures it off the note tails and convolves the MODEL to match before any metric is taken. Without that the release delta reads as seconds of pipe speech that no pipe has. `calibrate` measures the room at RT60 3.14 s, which is a nave and not a plate, so it is the instrument's own space rather than an effect anyone chose.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate`: the reference renders identically in real time and faster than it, and the same note twice is bit-identical, so there is no round robin to put a floor under the loss. The measured settle minimum is 250 ms. `realtime` is kept on anyway - the grid is 22 renders and the saving is under three minutes, while a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement.
_stimulus: A pipe holds until the key is released, so the gate only has to outlast the speech transient and give the steady state somewhere to be measured; the metrics take their sustain window between 0.6 s and 1.8 s after onset. What needs the length is the other end - a nave carries four seconds after the key comes up, and a tail cut short reads as a fast release.
_timbres: One registration per timbre, and two rather than one because the fit answers to the partial stack, which the pipe scale sets as much as the stop list does. They are named for what was measured and not for a school of building: which scaling a sampled organ was built to is not in the samples, and a label claiming it would be the one unverifiable line in a file whose whole point is that every number in it was measured.
_notes: Every sixth semitone across the manual compass. The extremes carry the ranks rather than the fundamental: at C2 the 16' rank is the lowest thing in the sound and at C7 the 1 3/5' is at 8 kHz, so an error in either is only visible at the end it lives at. A midrange-only grid would report a chorus that is wrong at both ends as correct.
_velocities: One. A pipe organ has no velocity response at all - the key opens a pallet and the wind either flows or does not - so a second point would measure the reference's MIDI implementation rather than the instrument. The harness reports the consequence rather than hiding it: with the velocity axis held fixed, `--diagnose` counts it off the probe rows and marks every dynamics knob unprobed instead of dead. That the model must also be flat across velocity is a claim worth checking separately, not a dimension to gate on.
_dimensions: Four exclusions, each measured rather than assumed. `tnr` is out because a rank below the played pitch is scored as noise by construction: the 16' sounds at f/2 and puts its partials at f/2, 3f/2, 5f/2, which is between the harmonics of f and so exactly where the measurement looks for noise. Taking the 16' from 0.42 to 0.02 leaves the partial stack and the brightness where they were, to within a rounding error, and moves tone-to-noise by 10 dB - every bit of that knob's reach on this dimension is the artefact. Gating on it would hold the voice to a bound that a registration decision moves and a defect does not. `damper` is out because with the building in the capture it measures the nave's RT60, and a bound recorded from a reverberation time fails on the day the model's release is finally right. `vel_range` is out because there is one velocity. `decay` is out because a chorus does not hold a steady level - its ranks beat against each other, and over the measured window that is 9.8 dB peak to peak at C2 - so the linear fit returns the beat's phase rather than a decay: the same note reads +5.1 dB/s over the first half of its own sustain and +0.8 over the second. The number is real and the modulation is part of the sound, but it is not a decay, and the model's ranks beat against a tuning the reference's know nothing about. `--w-env` should stay at zero in a fit here for the same reason. `stretch` is kept with a caveat: at C2 one FFT bin of the sustain window is about 22 cents, so the tuning column down there is quantisation as much as temperament.
_identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `pipe_organ.local.json`: the plugin's component triple and each timbre's preset. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/pipe_organ.json` and need nothing.
